why-rust-ownership-borrowing-and-the-men.r: A first Rust tool failed to compile after a variable was passed to a function and used again. The function took ownership of config, so it could not be used afterwards.
why-rust-ownership-borrowing-and-the-men.x: Ownership and borrowing let Rust prevent memory bugs without a garbage collector, and the compiler errors teach the rules.

errors-option-result-and-the-question-ma.r: A cleanup tool crashed on an unexpected file name and left a job half done. The code used unwrap on a file operation. It was changed to return a Result with context that names the path, the tool now reports the error and continues with the next file, and the exit code distinguishes partial failure from success.
errors-option-result-and-the-question-ma.x: Make failures part of the function type so callers must handle them, and keep panics for real bugs. Practise it on a scratch environment first.

structs-enums-traits-and-generics.r: A deploy tool reported a running service with no process id, because states were booleans and strings. The struct allowed is_running true with pid None, and unwrap panicked.
structs-enums-traits-and-generics.x: Enums and traits let you model valid states and share behaviour, so impossible states cannot be written.

cli-tools-with-clap-serde-and-files.r: A CI check built in Rust passed every build because it exited with zero on errors. The main function printed the error and returned normally. Changing it to return a Result from main made the process exit with a non zero code.
cli-tools-with-clap-serde-and-files.x: clap and serde turn structs into command lines and config files with little code, so focus effort on the logic.

async-rust-with-tokio-and-network-servic.r: An exporter stopped answering health checks when one handler read a large file. The handler used a blocking file read on the runtime thread, so with a few slow reads all workers were busy and health checks timed out.
async-rust-with-tokio-and-network-servic.x: Async Rust handles many connections in few threads, but one blocking call can stall everything. Practise it on a scratch environment first.

testing-cross-compilation-and-shipping-s.r: A tool built on a developer laptop failed on an older server with a missing library version. The binary was linked dynamically against a newer libc than the server had.
testing-cross-compilation-and-shipping-s.x: Ship a single static binary per target, built reproducibly in CI, so installation is copying one file.
